html:
The Battle of Crécy was fought on 26 August 1346 near Crécy-en-Ponthieu in northern France. An English army under King Edward III beat a much larger French army under King Philip VI.

It was an early battle of the Hundred Years' War. Edward had landed in Normandy in July and marched across northern France. With the French close behind, he stopped on a hillside and waited. His knights got off their horses and stood with the infantry, and thousands of archers with longbows were placed on the wings. The French arrived late in the day in disorder and attacked at once. Their hired Genoese crossbowmen were outshot and fell back. The French knights then rode through them and charged uphill, again and again, into a storm of arrows. None of the charges broke the line. Several thousand French died, among them many great nobles and the blind King John of Bohemia.

Edward went on to take the port of Calais, which England held for two centuries. Crécy showed that disciplined foot soldiers and archers could beat mounted knights, the masters of European war for 300 years. The Black Death soon stopped the fighting for a time.
sum: The Battle of Crécy was fought on 26 August 1346 near Crécy-en-Ponthieu in northern France. An English army under King Edward III beat a much larger French army under King Philip VI.
